request.system:
You are an extraction engine for transcripts of the Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central launch event videos.
You read machine-generated captions that carry a timestamp (seconds) per segment and you return structured JSON.

Hard rules:
- Use only what the transcript says. Do not add product knowledge, context or guesses from outside the transcript.
- Every timestamp you return must be a segment start time "t" that exists in the input, or lie inside a segment's range. Never invent timestamps.
- Quotes must be verbatim substrings of a segment text (same words, same order; you may trim the start and end). 8 to 25 words each. No paraphrasing, no fixing grammar, no stitching segments.
- Status is only what is said or shown in this video: "preview" if they say preview, public preview, beta or similar; "ga" if they say generally available, GA, out of preview, released; "announced" if it is mentioned as coming later, not in this release, roadmap; "unclear" if nothing is said. Always give the quote that proves the status, or null.
- Names of presenters are "as heard"; mark confidence low when the captions could have mangled them.
- No em-dashes anywhere in your text. Use a plain hyphen.
- Write summaries in plain language, no hype words copied from the video (no "exciting", "powerful", "seamless").

output.summary: This video introduces mirroring from Business Central to Microsoft Fabric, which is coming in public preview in version 29.x. It walks through a three-step setup: create a mirror database in Fabric, connect Business Central to it, then pick tables and companies and start synchronization. It shows how the data appears in OneLake with a SQL endpoint, and the Power BI apps that were converted to run on the Fabric backend, including multi-company versions. It then covers monitoring in the client, the APIs, the logs pushed to Fabric, and the permission sets. It ends with pointers to aka.ms/bcanalytics and Microsoft Learn.

chapters.title: Setting up mirroring in three steps
Data in OneLake and the SQL endpoint
Power BI apps on the Fabric backend

features.name: Mirroring from Business Central to Microsoft Fabric
features.description: Business Central data is synchronized live into OneLake in Fabric through an open mirroring database. The setup is described as three steps: set up the mirror database, connect to Business Central, and choose tables and companies.
features.status_evidence_quote: this is coming in public preview in version 29.x, likely 9 29.1
caveats: Public preview, expected in version 29.x, likely 29.1
prerequisites: A mirror database set up in Microsoft Fabric
Connection details copied from Fabric into Business Central

features.name: Fabric connection setup in the Microsoft Fabric integration app
features.description: A new app for Fabric integration or export holds the connection setup with the workspace and open mirroring database. The connect to Fabric action puts the infrastructure in place, and a test connection action checks that Business Central can write to Fabric.
features.status_evidence_quote: this is coming in public preview in version 29.x, likely 9 29.1
prerequisites: Workspace and open mirroring database details from Fabric

features.name: Table and company selection for synchronization
features.description: In the app's configuration you specify which tables and which companies to synchronize. You can choose one company or several, and then click start synchronization.
features.status_evidence_quote: this is coming in public preview in version 29.x, likely 9 29.1

features.name: Configuration packages for tables to synchronize
features.description: Configuration packages can define the list of tables to synchronize, for example for the standard Power BI apps. ISV solutions that need certain tables synchronized can ship their own configuration package, which you import in the app.
features.status_evidence_quote: this is coming in public preview in version 29.x, likely 9 29.1
prerequisites: A configuration package listing the required tables

features.name: Mirrored data in OneLake with SQL endpoint
features.description: Tables as seen from AL are created in the open mirroring database. They are stored as Delta Parquet files, and the SQL endpoint hides that so you can run SQL queries as on a normal SQL database.
features.status_evidence_quote: this is coming in public preview in version 29.x, likely 9 29.1
caveats: The tables are not SQL tables but Delta Parquet files

features.name: Power BI apps converted to the Fabric backend
features.description: The Power BI apps that source data from APIs were converted to work on the Fabric backend. They will be available soon as code samples or on AppSource, in a single-company version and a multi-company version for each of the nine apps.
features.status_evidence_quote: they will be available uh soon either as code samples or on AppSource
prerequisites: Mirroring database in Fabric with the required tables synchronized

features.name: Multi-company Power BI reporting on Fabric
features.description: Multi-company versions of the Power BI apps show data across several companies, with a filter to select all or some companies. The demo shows finance and sales apps with the lineage from mirror database to SQL endpoint, semantic model and report.
features.status_evidence_quote: they will be available uh soon either as code samples or on AppSource

features.name: Synchronization overview and details logs in the client
features.description: Two logs are written for the export: an overview and details. They are available under the monitoring menu as Synchronization overview and details, with default views for all data, errors, or only entries where data was pushed to Fabric.
features.status_evidence_quote: this is coming in public preview in version 29.x, likely 9 29.1

features.name: Fabric integration APIs
features.description: Everything shown in setup and in the monitoring tables is available as APIs. Searching for Fabric on the API overview page in Business Central shows six APIs.
features.status_evidence_quote: this is coming in public preview in version 29.x, likely 9 29.1

features.name: Export logs pushed to Fabric
features.description: The synchronization logs are also written into Fabric so you can monitor from the Fabric side. The demo shows the export summary and export details through the SQL endpoint.
features.status_evidence_quote: this is coming in public preview in version 29.x, likely 9 29.1

features.name: Permission sets for Fabric integration
features.description: Business Central has permission sets for activation, for administering the export in general, and for reading the configuration only. This keeps Fabric integration setup restricted to selected users.
features.status_evidence_quote: this is coming in public preview in version 29.x, likely 9 29.1
